name: Airtable Automations
description: Airtable Automations is an in-product workflow feature for configuring triggers and one or more actions that update Airtable data, run scripts, send notifications, or connect work across supported services.
agentUseSummary: Airtable Automations cannot be connected or installed as a separate Relay provider. Use the canonical Airtable provider only for its currently supported bounded base, record, and comment operations. Relay does not create, inspect, test, enable, disable, delete, or run automation definitions; store automation scripts or secrets; or call an incoming automation webhook until a dedicated product and security contract is approved. Approved Airtable record mutations may still activate automations that the customer has already configured, so downstream side effects remain the customer's Airtable configuration responsibility.

blocked.label: Create an Airtable Automations connection
blocked.description: Automations belongs to a base inside Airtable and does not publish a distinct provider identity, OAuth grant, callback, or resource lifecycle.

blocked.label: Manage automation definitions
blocked.description: Creating, viewing, duplicating, renaming, configuring, testing, enabling, disabling, updating, deleting, restoring, organizing, or subscribing to automations is not exposed through Relay's canonical Airtable API contract.

blocked.label: Trigger an automation directly
blocked.description: Relay does not call unique incoming-webhook URLs or use record mutations as an unmodeled automation execution API; webhook possession is bearer-like authority and Airtable does not verify request signatures.

blocked.label: Run scripts or handle automation secrets
blocked.description: Uploading or editing JavaScript, configuring inputs or outputs, making arbitrary fetch requests, reading logs, or storing and using Airtable automation secret values is blocked.

blocked.label: Administer automation usage
blocked.description: Run history, failure subscribers, ownership, base permissions, plan limits, AI actions, third-party accounts, billing, and workspace or enterprise administration remain outside this provider boundary.

blocked.label: Use private Airtable interfaces
blocked.description: Browser automation, sessions, cookies, passwords, verification codes, scraping, undocumented endpoints, private APIs, and arbitrary raw requests are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Airtable Automations action is enabled before a supported external contract and a safe trigger, side-effect, secret, and lifecycle policy are approved.

runtimeSupport.description: No Airtable Automations tools are mounted. OpenClaw may use only the canonical Airtable provider's approved bounded base, record, and comment tools.
No Airtable Automations tools are mounted. Hermes may use only the canonical Airtable provider's approved bounded base, record, and comment tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Airtable documents Automations as a trigger/action feature configured by base collaborators in its web and desktop product, with owner or creator permissions, plan-based run limits, run history, scripts, third-party actions, and enablement state. Relay's canonical Airtable OAuth scopes cover base schema, records, record comments, and user email, not automation definitions or runs. Existing record creates and updates may activate customer-configured automations as a provider-side consequence. Airtable also offers an incoming-webhook trigger through a unique URL, but anyone with that URL can invoke it, signature verification is unavailable, requests are limited to POST and 100 KB, and calls consume workspace automation runs. Relay has not approved that bearer-like URL as a credential or frozen its payload, side-effect, replay, audit, and revocation model.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep this feature slug non-installable and use canonical Airtable only for its explicit bounded operations, disclosing that record writes may trigger existing customer automations. If direct automation triggering becomes a product requirement, security, privacy, legal, runtime, and customer owners must approve one exact incoming-webhook contract with automation and base binding, encrypted URL storage, payload schema and redaction, approval and idempotency behavior, replay and abuse controls, run-limit handling, audit, rotation, revocation, downstream-action disclosure, failure behavior, and production acceptance. Do not implement automation management without a current documented OAuth API and least-privilege scopes from Airtable.

evidence.supports: Airtable presents Automations as an in-product no-code trigger and action system for workflows, notifications, integrations, and optional JavaScript.
Airtable documents base-level automation creation, trigger and action types, collaborator permissions, client platforms, monthly run limits, and the fact that record changes can initiate runs.
Airtable documents automation configuration, testing, enablement, duplication, deletion, subscribers, sections, and run history as signed-in product workflows.
Airtable assigns automation creation, deletion, duplication, configuration, and naming to base owners or creators while allowing broader collaborators to view configurations and copy URLs.
Airtable's incoming automation webhook uses a unique URL that anyone possessing can invoke, accepts bounded POST payloads, lacks signature verification, is rate-limited, and consumes automation runs.

Airtable documents automation scripts as background code configured inside a base, including secrets, input and output variables, external fetch, execution limits, and indirect triggering through record changes or API writes.
Airtable's public OAuth scope catalog exposes granular base, record, comment, webhook, user, enterprise, and related API authority without publishing an automation-definition or automation-run scope.
